The Australian mortgage market has "ballooned" due to banks issuing new loans against unrealized capital gains of existing investment properties, creating a $1.7 trillion "House of cards", according to a recent report. This system is described as a "Classic mortgage Ponzi finance model", with newly purchased properties often generating net rental income losses, adversely impacting upon cash flows.
In terms of property prices, Melbourne's median house price has risen by 12.7 per cent over the past year to $695,500, with Brisbane up 3 per cent to $488,757, Adelaide 5.2 per cent to $430,109, Hobart 13.6 per cent to $383,438 and Canberra 12.9 per cent to $575,173.
The Reserve Bank of Australia plays a significant role in monetary policy, with its setting of a target for the cash rate influencing short-term market rates and propagating throughout the market. Banks are profit-maximizes and will tend to move their home loan rates in the same direction, by broadly the same amount, at the same time.

history.content: Hi. I am planning to move to Australia. I do not want to pay rent. Could I buy a house there?

Yes, you can buy a house in Australia. It's essential to choose the location of house  carefully. If you buy a property in a good area that is well sought after, you can make good capital and rental returns over the long run. It is important to know that when you buy a property, the house or building goes down in value every year due to depreciation, but the land increases in value over time. The land value increases in sought-after areas where more people want to live.

Its primary weapon in this, is its setting of a target for the cash rate - the overnight money-market interest rate charged between financial intermediaries. Short-term market rates closely track this cash rate target, because the Reserve Bank controls the supply of funds that banks use to settle the transactions that use the overnight money-market interest rates. Australian capital markets are liquid, with many deposits / loans being on variable-rate or short-term rates; hence changes to the cash rate quickly propagate throughout the market. NB that the changes propagate, but not all interest rates are at the same level: the absolute values don't propagate.
